scenario: Community search over short user-generated posts, questions and comments. Key metrics: relevance (nDCG) and click-through rate. Focus: semantic matching, query understanding, retrieval, ranking and LLM applications.

papers.title: RemoteANN: A Native Vector Search Engine for Cloud Object Storage
papers.authors: Yutong Gou, Silu Huang, Yue Wang, Jianjun Chen, Cheng Long
papers.summary: RemoteANN co-designs vector indexing and query execution for cloud object storage. Quantized inverted lists, reordered data, merged range reads and local SSD caching reduce remote I/O. At matched target recall, the authors report up to 5.9× higher throughput than representative baselines.
papers.key_insight: The useful optimization target is remote requests per query. Data locality makes request merging and caching effective; faster distance computation alone cannot remove object-store latency.

papers.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
papers.authors: Liana Patel, Rishabh Ranjan, Ion Stoica, Matei Zaharia, Carlos Guestrin
papers.summary: TokenGate trains an existing model to skip less useful tokens in later layers. Token-gated attention supplies a learning signal for token selection. Across the tested tasks, the authors report up to 11.3× faster time to first token without measured accuracy loss.
papers.key_insight: Token selection can be learned during lightweight adaptation instead of imposed as a fixed heuristic. This targets prefill latency and memory, with an adaptation step required before deployment.

papers.title: KVCompass: A Discovery Plane for Internet-Scale Prefix Cache Sharing in LLM Serving
papers.authors: Shiyi Ling, Fei Fang, Chen Qian
papers.summary: KVCompass adds a discovery layer for reusable prompt-prefix caches across regions. It separates cache identity from placement and routes requests using reuse, load and network distance. Simulations and a three-continent testbed show up to a 14× reduction in P99 time to first token.
papers.key_insight: A prefix-cache directory must track changing holders rather than assume fixed placement. Cross-region routing also needs distance and load; a remote cache hit is not automatically cheaper than local recomputation.

papers.title: MOSAIC: Multi-Objective Search for Allocating Inference Cache Across LLM Decoder Layers
papers.summary: MOSAIC searches per-layer KV-cache budgets instead of allocating the same capacity everywhere. A single search maps the quality–memory tradeoff and transfers its allocation across total budgets. On the tested models, it matches uniform-allocation quality with up to 75% less cache.
papers.key_insight: Budget allocation is a separate design choice from token eviction. The learned plans favor a few middle layers and can sit on top of existing eviction methods.

papers.title: Announcing New vLLM and SGLang Inference Engines on TPU
papers.summary: Google introduces native PyTorch TPU backends for vLLM and SGLang. The engines retain framework schedulers and APIs while replacing lower-level kernels and cache transfers. Google reports more than 700 tokens/s for a single user with Kimi K3 on Ironwood in a specific configuration.
papers.key_insight: A platform plugin can preserve the serving control plane while specializing kernels and cache movement. The reported single-user speed is configuration-specific; concurrency and request lengths remain essential comparison inputs.

papers.title: SigmaTrace: Library-Agnostic Observability for CPU/GPU-Initiated RDMA Communication
papers.summary: SigmaTrace records individual RDMA operations below communication libraries and exposes GPU-initiated transfers. In the authors’ 128-GPU NCCL AllReduce test, host-side tracing adds 1.3% overhead.
papers.key_insight: Observability below the library layer can serve multiple frameworks. Per-operation traces distinguish traffic skew from synchronization delays; the quoted overhead applies specifically to host-side tracing.

papers.title: PACT: NVFP4 Data-Flow LoRA Fine-Tuning on Consumer GPUs
papers.authors: Lei Gao, Hossein Entezari Zarch, Chaoyi Jiang, Murali Annavaram
papers.summary: PACT accelerates frozen projections during LoRA training with native NVFP4 matrix operations and stores selected backward activations at low precision. Sensitive nonlinear operations keep higher-precision inputs. Evaluation spans multiple models and tasks on a 16GB RTX 5080; the abstract reports improvements without a single aggregate speedup figure.
papers.key_insight: LoRA reduces trainable state but does not eliminate frozen-weight compute or saved activations. PACT treats computation precision and activation-storage precision as separate choices.

papers.title: When Does Better Acceptance Pay? A Controlled Study of Speculative Decoding
papers.authors: Yongchao Long, Chunrui Zheng, Yuxuan Zhou, Guangkun Nie, Tian-Chi Ma, Chao Pang, Shuohuan Wang, Yuchen Ding, Xianbin Wen, Dianhai Yu, Junyuan Shang, Yuxi Zhou, Shenda Hong
papers.summary: This study tests when better draft acceptance actually improves speculative-decoding throughput. It retrains six drafter recipes on shared data and evaluates them across ten benchmarks with matched serving conditions. The preferred drafter and budget depend on task uncertainty and execution cost.
papers.key_insight: Accepted tokens per round is an intermediate metric. Compare useful tokens against round latency, and hold training data and inference settings constant before attributing gains to a new drafter.

papers.title: Integrating TorchTPU into TorchTitan and Optimizing Models for TPU
papers.summary: Google’s TorchTitan TPU integration brings collectives and full training steps into the compiler graph, then applies kernel and memory optimizations. In a weak-scaling experiment with fixed per-chip batch size, per-chip throughput drops about 8% as chip count grows 128-fold.
papers.key_insight: Communication becomes easier to overlap when it is visible inside the compiled graph. The scale result uses a growing global batch, so it measures framework scalability rather than fixed-batch training efficiency.

papers.title: Managed RAG search inside the sovereign perimeter: Gemini on GDC enterprise search
papers.summary: Google previews a managed RAG search stack that runs entirely inside an air-gapped GDC deployment. Local models, embeddings, PostgreSQL and object storage handle documents and persistent conversations. The stated per-file limit is 100MB; the announcement provides no comparative retrieval-quality benchmark.
papers.key_insight: Air-gapped deployment requires identity, ingestion, retrieval and conversation state to fit inside the same boundary. This is an architectural and capacity announcement, with limited comparative performance evidence.
